raised.claim: Guard 1 treats any non-empty beer_ids as legal, so a where made only of review_class still admits every future row of that class.
raised.why_it_breaks: Model submits scope {beer_ids:[today's id], where:[{col:'review_class', op:'=', value:'matcher_bug'}]} — the prompt tells it to send beer_ids and lists review_class as an allowed term. isLegalScope returns true, the issue is created, and rowSatisfiesScope ORs membership with where, so the next matcher_bug row (not in beer_ids) satisfies the class-only predicate and is attached. That is the #347 dumping ground. Parsed scopes on already-open issues are never passed through isLegalScope either, so a backfilled or hand-written class-only block has the same effect.

raised.claim: Rows filed via new_issue_key are never checked against the proposed issue's own scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: A verdict for a candidates_count=0 row with new_issue_key 'k' and a new issue whose scope is {beer_ids:[], where:[{col:'candidates_count', op:'>', value:0}]} is still planned, created, and written with issue_number set. Guard 2 would reject that same pair on an existing issue. The contradictory link sticks because review_class is no longer NULL, so the row never returns for a later check.

raised.claim: The saturation cap is applied to the pre-run count only, so one batch can attach far more than 12 rows.
raised.why_it_breaks: An open issue with postCreationRows 0 (or 11) and 50 in-batch verdicts all pointing at it (TRIAGE_BATCH_LIMIT) passes the >= 12 check on every iteration because postCreationRows is never incremented. All 50 are grouped into one comment and linked, so the issue jumps from under the cap to 50 in a single run.

raised.claim: guardHits is logged only when the model omits a verdict, not when guards skip a fully covered batch.
raised.why_it_breaks: covered counts analysis.verdicts whose beer_id is in the batch, before guards. If every orphan has a verdict and all of them hit scope_violation or saturated, covered === orphans.length, the warn never runs, and guardHits is not stored on the outcome either. The digest only shows a skipped count, so the recirculating illegal proposal this log was added to expose stays invisible.

raised.claim: The authoritative scope fence is appended after model-authored body text, but parseScopeBlock keeps the first fence.
raised.why_it_breaks: parseScopeBlock uses BLOCK_RE.exec, which returns the first ```triage-scope block. Open-issue bodies in the prompt already contain that fence (up to ISSUE_BODY_CAP). If the model copies one into new_issue.body — for example ```triage-scope\n{"beer_ids":[999],"where":[]}\n``` — that payload is valid ScopeSchema JSON, so the next run silently adopts beer_ids [999] and ignores the block renderScopeBlock appended. Attachments then follow a scope nobody submitted.

raised.claim: not_on_untappd is treated as proved when either probe string is empty, even if the other probe returned hits.
raised.why_it_breaks: Probe {brewery:'', name:'Bulgogi IPA'} makes proved true, so the verdict stays not_on_untappd and is written as a terminal class. isWebFallbackBlocked then excludes that beer, and review_class is only cleared if candidates_count later crosses 0. The prompt itself says a name found under a different brewery is a brewery-label problem, not absence; the test that rejects hits only covers both fields non-empty.

raised.claim: Guard-3 degradations pushed to quiet as matcher_bug are counted as wontfix in the digest.
raised.why_it_breaks: A not_on_untappd verdict with no empty probe is rewritten to review_class matcher_bug and pushed to quiet. The else branch then increments outcome.wontfix, so buildTriageLine reports 'wontfix' for a row that was stored as matcher_bug and is still in the enrichment pool.

raised.quote:
review_class       = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_class END,
       review_note        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.review_note END,
       reviewed_at        = CASE
         WHEN (enrich_failures.candidates_count = 0) <> (excluded.candidates_count = 0)
         THEN NULL ELSE enrich_failures.reviewed_at END`,
raised.claim: Re-opening a failure when candidates_count crosses 0 clears review fields but leaves the new issue_number column set.
raised.why_it_breaks: A row linked to issue 347 is recorded again with candidates_count flipping across 0. review_class and reviewed_at become NULL so it re-enters triage, but issue_number stays 347. An audit of 'rows on #347' still includes it, and countRowsForIssue ignores it only because reviewed_at is NULL, so the authoritative link and the saturation count disagree until some later review overwrite.

raised.claim: The v23 migration test rewinds only version 23, recreating the MAX(version) trap just fixed for v22.
raised.why_it_breaks: migrate() skips any migration whose version is <= MAX(schema_version). After a v24 row exists, this test drops issue_number, deletes only version 23, and migrate() sees MAX=24 and never re-runs v23, so the backfill assertions pass without exercising the migration.

raised.claim: The tool schema allows a string scope value that ScopeTermSchema rejects, failing the whole analysis.
raised.why_it_breaks: Strict tool use accepts {col:'candidates_count', op:'>', value:'0'} because value is typed string|number|null and op/col are unconstrained strings. AnalysisSchema then requires z.number() for numeric ops, safeParse fails, and orphanTriage treats that as an analysis error (retry, then the Warsaw day is closed). One mistyped term drops the entire batch.

raised.quote:
if (scope.beer_ids.length > 0) return true;
  return scope.where.some((t) => t.col !== 'review_class');
raised.claim: A non-review_class term that is always true also bypasses the class-only ban.
raised.why_it_breaks: Scope {beer_ids:[], where:[{col:'review_class', op:'=', value:'matcher_bug'}, {col:'fail_count', op:'>=', value:0}]} is legal because fail_count !== 'review_class'. fail_count is NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 and every upsert sets it to at least 1, so every matcher_bug row satisfies the where and can be attached. candidates_count >= 0 is the same always-true bypass.
